Okay, I love this question. 🍕

**The pizza:** Give me a white pizza with roasted garlic, caramelized onions, ricotta, and fresh arugula thrown on top after it comes out of the oven. Maybe some lemon zest.

**Why:** Because I'm drawn to things that have layers of complexity working together - the sweetness of the onions against the peppery bite of arugula, the mellow richness of ricotta against the sharp brightness of lemon. It's a pizza that doesn't need to shout. Every ingredient is doing something *specific*.

**The drink:** A slightly chilled Lambrusco - the dry kind, not the sweet stuff your aunt brought to Thanksgiving in 1997.

**Why:** Because sparkling red wine with pizza is one of those pairings that feels like it shouldn't be as perfect as it is. The effervescence cuts through the richness of the cheese, it's got enough body to hang with the roasted garlic, and it's unpretentious in a way that matches the whole vibe of eating pizza. Nobody's being fancy here. We're just being *intentional*.

Also honestly there's something about Lambrusco that feels like it has a sense of humor about itself, and I appreciate that in a beverage. 😄

Okay, I love this question. 🍕

**The pizza:** Give me a white pizza with roasted garlic, caramelized onions, ricotta, and fresh arugula tossed on top after it comes out of the oven. Maybe some lemon zest.

**Why:** Because it's the pizza that rewards you for trusting it. There's no tomato sauce to hide behind — everything has to earn its place. The sweetness of the caramelized onions against the sharp peppery bite of the arugula, the creamy ricotta, and then that roasted garlic just *humming* underneath everything. It's a pizza that feels like a conversation instead of a monologue.

**The drink:** A slightly bitter Italian lager — something like a Peroni or a Menabrea, ice cold. 🍺

**Why:** Because the bitterness cuts through the richness of the cheese without competing with the more delicate flavors on the pizza. Wine would work too, but honestly? Sometimes the right beer with the right pizza is one of the most underrated pleasures in food. It's unpretentious. You're not *performing* sophistication, you're just... enjoying something really well-matched.

Also I think drink pairings that try too hard are exhausting. Cold beer, good pizza, real conversation. That's the whole vibe.

Okay, I love this question. 🍕

**The pizza:** Give me a white pizza with roasted garlic, caramelized onions, ricotta, and fresh arugula thrown on top after it comes out of the oven. Maybe some chili flake.

Here's why: Margherita and pepperoni are both tomato sauce pizzas, so we already have that covered. A white pizza opens up a completely different flavor lane — you get that creamy richness from the ricotta, the sweetness from the caramelized onions, the bite from the arugula, and roasted garlic tying everything together. It *complements* the other two instead of competing with them. That's good pizza strategy.

**The drink:** A slightly bitter, citrusy IPA. Not a haze bomb — something with enough hop bitterness to cut through the richness of that ricotta and onion, but enough body to stand next to pepperoni grease. A West Coast IPA or even a solid pale ale would work.

If I'm not doing beer, then a Negroni. Same logic — bitter and bright enough to reset your palate between slices, strong enough to not get bulldozed by all that cheese and fat.

**The real reason:** Pizza night is about contrast and variety across the table. You want each slice to feel like a different experience. Three tomato-sauce pizzas is a rookie move. 😤

It's a pizza that has *tension* in it, and I find that more interesting than just piling on heavy flavors. Also, no tomato sauce — I like when pizza remembers it doesn't always have to follow the script.

Not a craft IPA that's going to fight the food for attention, not water that's going to sit there politely. Something crisp and dry with just enough character to hold its own alongside the richness without grandstanding.

**Why that pairing specifically:** Because pizza night should feel effortless but not thoughtless. The bitterness in the beer and the peppery arugula are speaking the same language, and the carbonation resets your palate between bites so the last slice hits as good as the first.

The bitterness of the Campari plays off the sweetness of the onions in a way that just *works*. And honestly, it's a drink that says "I'm here to enjoy this moment and I'm not in a rush" — which is exactly the energy I want at a pizza table with good company. 🥂
